cells.tense: Here, the moving and the feeling have found the same speed, and you are with the pen.
cells.act: eat the meal you made and leave the kitchen as it is
cells.ask: After your next dinner, leave the pots and the crumbs where they sit. Sit down somewhere else for ten minutes. Tomorrow's kitchen can start tomorrow.
cells.core:
You move at a pace that doesn't need defending, and what you feel and what you do agree about the direction. That agreement is doing the work — no gritting through, no convincing yourself. A good day is one where you finish something and feel satisfied without immediately planning the next thing.

That satisfaction is what's free to feed now. After your next dinner, leave the pots where they sit, sit down somewhere else, and let ten minutes pass before you touch anything. You may find the evening feels wider than usual. That's what a finished thing does when you don't instantly reach past it — it gives you the hour back.
cells.sheetLine: You finish and don't reach for the next thing.
cells.verb: moving at the pace where will and feeling have stopped arguing
cells.place: in the part of life that is becoming what it already is

cells.tense: You are already living past the next turn, bracing for a shape you can't write in yet.
cells.act: gather the scattered thoughts into one line
cells.ask: Take a sheet of paper and put whatever's circling in your head down as a single sentence — what you actually want next. Fold it. Stop looking at it.
cells.core:
You're moving, and part of you is already several moves ahead, checking whether the ground will hold. The bracing is real, and it's costing you the ease this pace usually gives. A good day is one where you don't need to know the next hour before you take the next step.

The trouble isn't thinking ahead. It's that the thinking has scattered into a dozen worries wearing the same face. Put the scattered thing down as a single sentence — what you actually want next, not what might go wrong — fold it, and stop looking at it. The ground holds more than your worry about it does, and you'll find that out by walking, not by checking.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing for a turn you can't see yet.
cells.verb: moving at the pace where will and feeling have stopped arguing
cells.place: in the part of life that is becoming what it already is

cells.tense: You are at a door that is already behind you, and the momentum has gone quiet.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: Think of something that ended this past year. List three things it left you. Keep the page somewhere. You don't have to use it for anything.
cells.core:
You're not moving much, and it's not because nothing matters. Something changed or ended, and you're still where it used to be, waiting for a signal that already came. The fire that usually moves you is low, and it's hard to feel the difference between rest and being stuck.

What's waiting is the gathering. Bring back something that ended this past year — a job, a place, a way you spent your days — and list three things it left you. Not what you lost. What it handed over on the way out. Keep the page. You don't have to do anything with it. Counting is the whole act.
cells.sheetLine: You're waiting at a door that already closed.
cells.verb: moving at the pace where will and feeling have stopped arguing
cells.place: in the part of life that is becoming what it already is

cells.tense: You are building something daily and calling it the job, the habit, or just what you do.
cells.act: commit to the long build and do today's part
cells.ask: Picture the thing you keep coming back to as it would look after a year of this, and put that picture somewhere you can see it. Then do today's part of it, and not one step more.
cells.core:
You keep showing up to something — day after day, quiet, persistent. You'd probably say it's just the work, or the routine, or what needs doing. But something in you chose that, and keeps choosing it. A good stretch is one where the showing up feels like yours and not like the calendar's.

The build is yours. Picture the thing you keep coming back to as it would look after a year of this, and put that picture somewhere you can see it. Then do today's part of it. Not more, not a plan. Just the part that belongs to today. Seeing the year is the acknowledgment; the doing is already in your hands.
cells.sheetLine: The thing you keep building is yours.
cells.verb: moving at the pace where will and feeling have stopped arguing
cells.place: in the part of life that is becoming what it already is
